svg.title: Desk node on the LABTECH 9 x 15 dot board
svg.text: TOP side (white grid, LABTECH print) - row numbers on your LEFT, 001 at the top. Parts and wires go in from here.
The letters are printed for the other face, so they read mirrored here; count columns from the numbered edge (white lines every 5). Solid = this side, dashed = underneath.
rows 025-050: kept free for the 12 V stage (IRL540N, 100 ohm, 10 k, 12 V pigtail) - later, gate from D25 = P010
green link: round the top end, over the red and black links
470 ohm standing on L010; its top leg slants down into J010, sleeved
1000 uF: LONG leg L016 on the +5V bus, striped SHORT leg J016
LED 1 end: green DIN wire J011
lash: bare wire through E004 and E012, over the bundle
UNDERSIDE (copper rings) - turned over left-to-right like a page. Letters now read normally, numbers on the RIGHT.
This is the face you solder. Every joint is a dot or a ring. Coordinates are letter + printed row, e.g. L010 = column L, row 010.
no ESP32 on this side: 30 header pins to solder
rows 025-050: kept free for the 12 V stage (IRL540N, 100 ohm, 10 k, 12 V pigtail) - later, gate from D25 = P010
link ends: through O003 and O004, bent onto the VIN and GND pins
N008: diode band leg + green link end from O008, one joint
green link's other end from A'008, bent onto the RX2 pin Z008
junction: diode's plain leg down J008-J011, cut past J011
1000 uF short leg from J016 to the GND bus at H016
solid dots: soldered at step 2. Rings: soldered when that leg arrives
thick red / dark grey: a BUS - one bare wire along the pads on the underside, laid beside the hole centres. Dashed in the top view because it is underneath
thin solid green / red / black (top view): an insulated link on this side; its end goes through the hole NEXT to the pin and is bent onto the pin underneath
amber: the diode's own plain leg, bent along four pads under the board. The 470 ohm and the green DIN wire go through beside it and solder to it
Key columns, counted from the numbered edge: 4 = A' 5 = Z (left header) 15 = P (right header) 16 = O 17 = N 19 = L (+5V bus) 21 = J (junction) 23 = H (GND bus) 26 = E
Only three ESP32 pins are used: VIN = P003, the GND below it = P004, RX2 = Z008. Nothing goes to 3V3 or the other GND. The board is not cut.
Nothing bare may reach from one bus to the other. Between them there are only three things:
the junction (column J), the capacitor leg into the GND bus, and the two legs of the 0.1 uF.
